answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may earn reputation or claim work. A newcomer posts an anchor bond, then builds trust through completed jobs; if it cheats, disputes can trigger a loss of that bond and invalidate its reputation. Splitting into many identities does not create free influence: each one needs its own capital, while honest agents can grow a vine of referrals from proven work. The oasis of low-cost fake accounts disappears, replaced by a real upfront cost and risk of forfeiture.
